artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Kill the Wolf is the fourth studio album from English comedian and musician Matt Berry, originally released in July 2013 on Acid Jazz Records. The album showcases Berry's eclectic approach to songwriting, blending progressive rock, folk, and pop sensibilities across twelve tracks. Songs like "Gather Up," "Devil Inside Me," and "Fallen Angel" demonstrate his ability to craft introspective compositions, while longer pieces such as "Solstice" (9:26) reveal his ambition toward expansive, album-oriented arrangements. The record finds Berry in a contemplative mood, building on the foundation established by his earlier work.

Within Berry's discography, Kill the Wolf represents a continuation of his artistic evolution following Witchazel, maintaining his distinctive blend of folk-influenced melodies and rock instrumentation. The album's track listing, which includes contributions from collaborators like Cecilia Fage on "Wolf Quartet," demonstrates Berry's willingness to work with other musicians while maintaining creative control over the majority of the material. The album's runtime and varied song structures—ranging from brief interludes to extended compositions—reflect a progressive sensibility that aligns with the album's categorization as both folk rock and progressive rock.

The album received moderate critical attention, earning a Metacritic score of 71/100, indicating generally favorable reviews from music publications. A 10th Anniversary Edition was released in June 2023, featuring the original album tracks alongside selected bonus material, introducing Kill the Wolf to a new generation of listeners and affirming its enduring place within Berry's catalog.
